clue.text: Rest-rota men organised in in protest

indicators.note: letters that are organised are put into a new order, so these words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Staff on a rest rota band together to make a complaint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organised' rearranges the eleven letters of REST-ROTA MEN. The clue prints 'in' twice; both are link words before the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To remonstrate is to object forcefully, which is a synonym of protest as a verb.

clue.text: Doesn't tolerate lies about Indian Sikh leaders

indicators.note: about means one word goes round the letters the leaders supply

parts.note: to lie is to rest, so lies gives rests

indicators.note: the leaders of Indian and Sikh are their opening letters

explanation.surface: Someone refuses to put up with untruths told about Indian Sikh leaders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts IS (from 'Indian Sikh leaders') inside RESTS, splitting it as RES-IS-TS.
explanation.definitionFit: To resist something is to refuse to accept or put up with it.

clue.text: Wooden man, soft at heart

indicators.note: at heart means the letter goes into the middle of the other word

parts.note: a man is a male
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning soft

explanation.surface: A stiff, wooden fellow who is really gentle underneath.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at heart' puts P into the middle of MALE. 'Wooden' is the definition in the sense of made of a particular wood, as in maple furniture.
explanation.definitionFit: Maple is a hardwood used for furniture, so a maple table is a wooden one of that timber.

clue.text: A small number shatter, possibly a quarter

parts.note: NO is the short form of number

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters may be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A handful of things break, perhaps in one district of town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges NO plus SHATTER. 'quarter' here is a point of the compass, not a district.
explanation.definitionFit: The compass is divided into quarters, and the north-east is one such direction between north and east.

clue.text: The art gallery is in debt a temporary setback

indicators.note: is in says the answer sits inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A national gallery's money troubles are only a passing blip.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'debT A TEmporary'. The TATE is the group of national art galleries in Britain, the best known in London.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tate is a famous group of British public galleries of modern and historic art.

clue.text: A job for the summer

parts.note: the summer here is one who sums, an adder of figures, and their task is the work of totting up

explanation.surface: Someone looks for seasonal work during the hot months.
explanation.walkthrough: 'summer' reads as the season but means a person who does sums.
explanation.definitionFit: Totting up numbers is the arithmetic task that a person who sums carries out.

clue.text: He'll order a great dish

definitions.meaning: one who charges, who gives commands, as in charging someone to do a task

explanation.surface: A diner will ask for a big plate of food.
explanation.definitionFit: To charge is to command, so one who does so commands; separately a large platter for meat is called by this old name.

clue.text: A novice will take ale with spirits in it

indicators.note: this word is a container marker: it says one piece is placed inside the other, and the clue words of the pieces show which way round
with it in it means one word is placed inside the other

parts.note: ale is a kind of beer
ginn, also spelt jinn, are spirits in Arabic folklore

explanation.surface: A newcomer to drink will order beer laced with gin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spirits' looks like gin alone but gives GINN, the genies of Arabian tales; 'with ... in it' places GINN inside BEER.
explanation.definitionFit: A beginner is someone just starting out, a learner or newcomer.

clue.text: Copies taken back, appraised, and broken up

indicators.note: taken back means the word is read from right to left

parts.note: to copy is to ape, so copies gives apes
to appraise is to rate

explanation.surface: Reproductions are returned, valued and then split apart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken back' turns APES into SEPA, then RATED follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that have been separated have been parted or split from each other.

clue.text: Lists some rare natural phenomena

indicators.note: some means only part of the following words is used

explanation.surface: A catalogue includes several unusual events in nature.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'rARE NAtural'. 'Lists' looks like a verb or plural noun of catalogues; the lists were the enclosed ground for medieval jousting.
explanation.definitionFit: The lists were the fenced field for tournaments, an enclosure for contests.

clue.text: Look at the bubble

parts.note: to look at something is to see it

explanation.surface: Someone is told to watch a bubble.
explanation.definitionFit: To seethe is to boil or foam, so liquid that does so bubbles.

clue.text: Giving guidance, though always in pain

indicators.note: in means one word is put inside the other

parts.note: a sting is a sharp pain
e'er is the poetic short form of ever, meaning always

explanation.surface: Someone offers advice while constantly suffering.
explanation.definitionFit: Steering means directing a course, which is guiding someone or something along.

clue.text: Sort of beetle cicatrice on a seaman

parts.note: a cicatrice is the mark left by a healed wound
AB stands for able seaman

explanation.surface: A sailor bears a scar of some beetle kind.
explanation.definitionFit: The scarab is a dung beetle, sacred in ancient Egypt.

clue.text: Capital dumped in a river

indicators.note: in means one word is placed inside the other

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Scotland, and another in Wales and England
something dumped has been laid down

explanation.surface: Something valuable was thrown into a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' looks like money but is a state capital; 'in' puts LAID inside A DEE.
explanation.definitionFit: Adelaide is the chief city of the state of South Australia.

clue.text: More often to be found at Westminster

definitions.meaning: more usual or more frequently met
a member of the House of Commons, which sits at Westminster in London

explanation.surface: Someone is frequently seen around the Houses of Parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: The comparative of common means more usual; also an MP in the elected lower house sits in the Commons.

clue.text: One following a famed eccentric grimaced

indicators.note: following means the second piece comes after the first
eccentric means odd, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: an ace is the card standing for one

explanation.surface: A well-known oddball's companion pulled a face.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eccentric' rearranges A FAMED into MADEAF, which ACE follows.
explanation.definitionFit: To pull a face of disgust or pain is to grimace.

clue.text: The bookbinder's death-certificate?

parts.note: a document recording an end, as a bookbinder might describe the blank leaf glued at the close of a book

explanation.surface: A craftsman who binds books has a paper recording someone's death.
explanation.walkthrough: A death certificate marks an end; in bookbinding the leaves pasted inside the covers carry that name.
explanation.definitionFit: Bookbinders paste a blank folded sheet inside each cover, joining the book block to the binding.

clue.text: One voter may make a suggestion

indicators.note: may make signals that the letters can be formed into something new

explanation.surface: A single elector might put forward an idea.
explanation.definitionFit: An overtone is an implication or hint beyond the literal meaning.

clue.text: Notice to keep

definitions.meaning: to notice is to see or remark
to keep a rule or festival, to follow it

explanation.surface: A sign announcing what is to be retained.
explanation.definitionFit: Observing means seeing or perceiving; it also means honouring a custom such as a sabbath.

clue.text: A Communist holding the party is much admired

indicators.note: holding means one piece contains the other

parts.note: Red is the traditional label for a Communist
a do is an informal party

explanation.surface: A left-wing politician at the event is greatly popular.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding' puts DO inside A RED, after the A.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone adored is loved deeply, worshipped by fans.

clue.text: The writer knows detectives must return first

indicators.note: first means this piece comes at the start of the answer
must return says the letters are read backwards

parts.note: CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, the detective branch of British police
to ken is to know, an old and Scottish word

explanation.surface: An author is aware that the police investigators have to come back before anything else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'must return' turns CID into DIC, which 'first' puts before KENS.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles Dickens was the Victorian novelist of Oliver Twist and Bleak House.

clue.text: Picture painted in water colours

parts.note: water colours suggests the medium, but read it as a painting coloured with water, a view of the ocean

explanation.surface: A watercolour painting is described.
explanation.walkthrough: 'water colours' looks like the medium of the painting; it describes the subject, the ocean's colours.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a painting whose subject is a view of the ocean.

clue.text: Inexpensive variety of peach

indicators.note: a variety of something is a different form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A low-priced kind of fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheap goods cost little money.

clue.text: Scholars with nervous trouble needed something filling

parts.note: MAs are holders of a Master of Arts degree
a tic is a nervous twitch

explanation.surface: Academics with a twitch need a hearty meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'something filling' suggests food but means a filler such as a putty or cement.
explanation.definitionFit: Mastic is a resin or putty used as a sealant to fill gaps.

clue.text: Rear coaches

definitions.meaning: to rear is to bring up or ... a child or animal

explanation.surface: The back carriages of a vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: To rear a young creature is to bring it up and school it; a line of railway carriages forms a locomotive-drawn set.

clue.text: A stud manager

definitions.meaning: a knob or raised ornament on a surface
the person in charge at work

explanation.surface: A horse-breeding farm and the person who runs it.
explanation.definitionFit: A raised knob on a shield is a stud; the person in charge at work is the head or chief.

clue.text: Relieve back for example, spine

parts.note: to relieve someone of something is to rid them of it

indicators.note: back means the letters are turned around

parts.note: EG is the short form of exempli gratia, for example

explanation.surface: Ease a sore back, for instance the spine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns EG into GE; 'back' looks like part of the anatomy alongside 'spine'.
explanation.definitionFit: A ridge is a long raised crest, like the backbone of a hill or roof.

clue.text: Generate support by a football crowd

parts.note: a prop is a support
the gate is the number of spectators at a match

explanation.surface: Fans at a football match produce encouragement.
explanation.definitionFit: To propagate is to breed or produce more of something.

clue.text: Frenchwomen seen in pairs going to the dogs

indicators.note: going to the dogs means falling into ruin, so the letters are wrecked and rearranged

explanation.surface: Women from France are spotted two by two at the greyhound races.
explanation.definitionFit: Women from the French capital are called by this feminine plural noun.
